title: Gapped text: Why Do We Yawn?

passages.title: Why Do We Yawn?
passages.intro: 5 sentences have been removed. Choose the sentence that best fits each gap. There is one extra sentence you do not need.
passages.credit: Original text written for this practice.
paragraphs: Everybody yawns. Babies yawn before they are even born, and so do dogs, cats, snakes and fish. [[1]] Surprisingly, scientists still cannot agree on the answer.
For a long time, people believed we yawn because our bodies need more oxygen. [[2]] When volunteers breathed air with extra oxygen, they yawned just as often as before.
A newer idea is that yawning cools the brain. [[3]] Supporters of this theory point out that people yawn more in spring and autumn than on very hot days, when the air is too warm to cool anything.
Then there is the strangest thing about yawning: it is catching. [[4]] Some studies have found that we are more likely to catch a yawn from family and friends than from strangers.
[[5]] It may even help a group stay alert together. Whatever the reason, you have probably yawned at least once while reading this.

bank.A: Seeing, hearing or even reading about someone yawning can make you yawn too.
bank.B: So why do we do it?
bank.C: Taking a deep breath of air draws cooler blood towards the head, like a radiator.
bank.D: This suggests that contagious yawning may be linked to how much we care about others.
bank.E: Some people believe yawning is rude.
bank.F: But experiments have not supported this explanation.
